column1:
- Policy stance: The Sep 21, 2022 FOMC statement is clearly hawkish—another 75 bp hike to 3–3.25%, guidance for “ongoing increases,” and continued balance sheet runoff—tilting negatively for growth and risk assets.
- Credit conditions: The July 2022 SLOOS shows broad tightening in bank lending standards and terms for C&I and CRE, plus tighter household credit in several categories, with weaker CRE loan demand—adding a drag to activity.
- Beige Book (August 2022) overlay:
  - Activity mixed/flat overall; New York notes rising recession risk even as employment continues to increase and tourism remains a relative bright spot.
  - Financial institutions report mixed-to-softer demand in commercial/industrial lending, consistent with tighter standards.
  - Some easing in input prices (steel, lumber, copper reported in Boston and other districts) modestly tempers inflation pressures, but overall price levels remain elevated.
- Net effect: The Beige Book largely corroborates softer demand and tighter credit with only modest offsets (tourism resilience, some commodity price relief). Relative to the SLOOS-only view, this nudges the outlook a bit more negative.
